tools.name: search_stays
tools.description: Find hotels with a room free for the dates and guests. Returns each stay's cheapest fitting room with a quote (price, ATA fee 5%, typical 15-20% OTA cut). Demo hotels are marked demo: true.

tools.name: get_stay
tools.description: Rooms, prices, what's included, check-in/out times and cancellation terms for one stay. Demo hotels are marked demo: true.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: Re-check one room for exact dates and guests right before booking. Returns available yes/no and the live quote. Demo hotels are marked demo: true.

tools.name: book_direct
tools.description: Places a 15-minute HOLD on the room and emails the guest a 6-digit code. Nothing is booked and nothing reaches the hotel until the guest confirms. tools.name: confirm_booking
tools.description: Confirm a held booking with the 6-digit code the guest received by email. Only use a code the guest gave you. Five wrong codes cancel the hold. Confirming twice returns the same booking.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "book_direct" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Places a 15-minute HOLD on the room and emails the guest a 6-digit code. Nothing is booked and nothing reaches the hotel until the guest confirms. After calling…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: book_direct · Public sink: book_direct, confirm_booking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: book_direct · Public sink: book_direct, confirm_booking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
